title: Race Cars Zoom Past the White House!
summary:
Have you ever seen a race car zoom past the White House? On August 23, 2026, that really happened! The first-ever IndyCar street race in Washington, D.C. turned famous roads like Pennsylvania Avenue into a race track. Tens of thousands of people packed the National Mall to watch.

And guess what? A real bald eagle flew over the track during the singing of 'God Bless America'! People wore red, white, and blue hats, shirts, and even earrings. Some wore shirts with bald eagles on them. One fan, Cameron Graves, wore American flag pants and said the event was 'patriotic and electric.'

The winner was Kyle Kirkwood from Florida. He drove his #27 Sam's Club Honda and led 128 of the 147 laps. That's a big win! He celebrated with his crew after the race.

Before the race, President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump took a ride in the presidential limousine, called 'The Beast.' Then President Trump waved the green flag to start the race. Crowds cheered and chanted 'U.S.A.'

The race was part of a big celebration for America's 250th birthday. There were military bands and flyovers, including the new Air Force One. It was a weekend full of speed, flags, and fun. Would you want to watch a race on those famous streets?
why_it_matters: This story shows how a big national celebration can bring people together for fun events right in front of famous landmarks — something you might see or take part in someday.
